Our deadline is in just a few hours, and this is the last call for donations before we close the books on November
#
Derek, victories don’t come easy.
It took a hell of a lot of work back in 2020 to kick Trump to the curb. VoteVets mobilized Veterans, we fought disinformation, we ran some of the hardest-hitting ads in the business, and even still — it could easily have gone against us.
And in 2022, we pushed extremely hard. We minimized our losses in the House and actually gained seats in the Senate.
Since then we’ve gotten results down-ballot, turning over school boards, mayoral seats, state legislatures, and more. We’re investing heavily in infrastructure now that will pay dividends in the final weeks and months of 2024.
**[And today, on our end-of-month deadline, we’re asking you to make your first donation to support that work.**](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-nov23.rp0I1d&refcode=em231130-1-30&t=1&akid=19889%2E3013755%2E4h9NXf)
Our deadline is in just a few hours, and this is the last call for donations before we close the books on November and turn the page to December. An FEC reporting month — the most important month of the year.
At the end of December we’ll need to report out everything we’ve raised and spent over the full year. Putting up a strong report could scare some challengers off. It’ll mean we can do more to support strong candidates. We can spend more on ads, organizing, you name it.
But if we don’t raise what we need to, we have to scale back. Frankly... it could be a disaster. A lot of folks are counting on us. And we aim to deliver for them. That’s our duty.
This is important, Derek.
**[So, one more time, we’re asking you to chip in before our deadline tonight. Make it for $5, make it for whatever you can. _**"The problem is that Democrats' 2024 Senate challenges go far beyond West Virginia. They face such a starkly unfavorable map that, if things even go somewhat poorly for the party, they could fall into a deep Senate hole for years to come."**_
Fellow Conservative,

With Joe Manchin out, the Senate runs directly through Montana. And this means that we have our work cut out for ourselves. **[Let me give you a couple of reasons why Joe Manchin's retirement announcement elevates our race to the top spot:](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=4626a94609334f5e827bd07cd1f93763&_e=dSirXDyRyhDhgtvospChXEfDUI7KvJVa3F7J2LcZ5Kc3RX_xsQ6wkYO2mKImWxqE9qPxUGRqUZjVLeLvSaPVhBfU6rM81A0blJnI_yAppKhSK9FwoRnf0AZTiUr8F9JFWwRo5GInTqbmG6kvCzdpCwveRVwtpWd5zACfCHuhBDQNLeG5ID3zRwcjdjAuffHxy1Hj4csef38i42FW4SDuVuwsaIP-14UvE-QZhRFJ9jdyab1JgdvpQlsRNZQLyGcToP1Fu4dkhPUcahjt4D-8Zu4_t-RjqTgECmktX5iztIxx3ZsWIv1Cd2_ByvNkVwZpk4xnTDAFgcPQP__oFuNJUKyBr9l2YQf0hvoFrhQdhlmSMl8wl6rdWFCBnx6-eAWvD-D6Sf_E9tnQCsOnlOrRPw%3D%3D)**
* Chuck Schumer no longer has to decide where to put his resources–they're coming to Montana. With Joe Manchin out of the race, Schumer will all but write off West Virginia, ceding the seat to Republicans. Manchin's retirement will likely free up between $25-$50 million in defense funds for the Democrats. **[[link to donate]](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=4626a94609334f5e827bd07cd1f93763&_e=dSirXDyRyhDhgtvospChXEfDUI7KvJVa3F7J2LcZ5Kc3RX_xsQ6wkYO2mKImWxqE9qPxUGRqUZjVLeLvSaPVhBfU6rM81A0blJnI_yAppKhSK9FwoRnf0AZTiUr8F9JFWwRo5GInTqbmG6kvCzdpCwveRVwtpWd5zACfCHuhBDQNLeG5ID3zRwcjdjAuffHxy1Hj4csef38i42FW4SDuVuwsaIP-14UvE-QZhRFJ9jdyab1JgdvpQlsRNZQLyGcTWC3bYlorcYd8oWV17XEFMr_gqbPMIKHZuyCivxuAk8mbMjlya6vhqOfzEEii5huhnqR_JTvBhRfLHDYODyinLWMI13EATlOcTolL-slHWADRbZD2p_6SR1L6bmnGVNvJs9DWs-kIVwX__E93dawNng%3D%3D)**

* Schumer won't have to persuade wealthy coastal donors into donating to a Manchin reelection effort. Instead of choosing between protecting Manchin or Tester - or contributing to both candidates - they'll be donating the maximum amount only to Tester. Coastal donors have helped Tester shatter Montana fundraising records each quarter, accumulating $15 million in donations since January 1st. I need help catching up because, to be frank, we haven't brought in a fraction of this from our online community. [**[link to donate]**](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=4626a94609334f5e827bd07cd1f93763&_e=dSirXDyRyhDhgtvospChXEfDUI7KvJVa3F7J2LcZ5Kc3RX_xsQ6wkYO2mKImWxqE9qPxUGRqUZjVLeLvSaPVhBfU6rM81A0blJnI_yAppKhSK9FwoRnf0AZTiUr8F9JFWwRo5GInTqbmG6kvCzdpCwveRVwtpWd5zACfCHuhBDQNLeG5ID3zRwcjdjAuffHxy1Hj4csef38i42FW4SDuVuwsaIP-14UvE-QZhRFJ9jdyab1JgdvpQlsRNZQLyGcTHN8apfUBAN_qIvSJ_JnAgQ6zusGaEgKE1XEtlUeBI_KU7hGsTdskehvffCnk0Q5MQ9o3VRyv5MmLAlcF53A_r5khT_8Gu2mvdOXbRBsDFdtxb6ghTy41Kp3sDC8QvAOAasf33SgNDgWlwAhc8l3PAg%3D%3D)

* The other Democrat incumbents up for reelection this year are from states Biden won in 2020. That doesn't necessarily mean Republicans don't have a shot to win these races, but the incumbents aren't as likely to need as much money to win as my opponent will.

All of these things, taken together, mean that Jon Tester is about to become the recipient of some MAJOR cash. And while that alone doesn't guarantee he'll find a way to extend his nearly quarter-century political career, he might be able to buy (_**read lie**_) his way to reelection if he raises $200,000,000+.

**[I need your help. Sincerely.](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=4626a94609334f5e827bd07cd1f93763&_e=dSirXDyRyhDhgtvospChXEfDUI7KvJVa3F7J2LcZ5Kc3RX_xsQ6wkYO2mKImWxqE9qPxUGRqUZjVLeLvSaPVhBfU6rM81A0blJnI_yAppKhSK9FwoRnf0AZTiUr8F9JFWwRo5GInTqbmG6kvCzdpCwveRVwtpWd5zACfCHuhBDQNLeG5ID3zRwcjdjAuffHxy1Hj4csef38i42FW4SDuVuwsaIP-14UvE-QZhRFJ9jdyab1JgdvpQlsRNZQLyGcTGYQnyd1ADCTunCKzUIn7UcvH7x-bn6Ks0N2hh-Hg_lDO1ery251FKo-jKOB3sOFUsFL5XMgP_ivZxzcyDLxHgzjVooRRDfJyytO-Dp_1lJ_SxHZwqeLrbWhJv9wkug7Qxaas2KUfia99xhbwAk-OGQ%3D%3D)** I may not be a household name but feel free to google me, my race, or my opponent's name, and you'll see the endless articles written about our race this year. **It's going to be a big.**

We have everything going for us except one thing: **money.**

1. Running against a liberal incumbent in Trump country: **check**
2. Endorsements from Montana's conservative elected officials: **check**

Friend,
Once the steel capital of the West, Pueblo powered our state and our country for decades. But like many American cities, Pueblo paid the price for a 40-year Washington consensus that stretches back to Ronald Reagan.
It's easy to summarize: National Republicans cut taxes for the wealthiest Americans and corporations, which slashed investments in the American people, and companies shipped our supply chains and jobs overseas.
Americans have rejected this agenda, and we’ve begun to chart a new course.
We passed the Inflation Reduction Act – the most significant climate legislation that any country on the planet has ever passed.
Unfortunately, not every leader in Colorado supports this progress. Lauren Boebert voted against the Inflation Reduction Act — the law that’s bringing hundreds of good-paying jobs to her district.
Because of this bill, the United States is better positioned than any country in the world to lead the global transition to clean energy. And there is no state in America better positioned to lead the country in our transition than Colorado.
Yesterday, President Biden toured CS Wind in Colorado, the world's largest manufacturing plant for wind turbines, which plans to expand as a result of the Inflation Reduction Act. This expansion will create over 800 new good-paying jobs in Pueblo.

body:
Peter,
My team just crunched the numbers, and we still have $2,526 remaining until we reach our $15,000 online fundraising goal for the month. If you’re able to help us catch up before tonight’s deadline, here’s a link for you: [_**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/BBVT-ALL-Email-Nov2023-FR-EOM**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/74327888/441315653/1816501303?refcode=E5337-20231130-EOM3-SL-DeadlineEOM&amount=27&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyNjM5ZDRhMS1kMDhmLWVlMTEtODkyNS0wMDIyNDgyMjNmMzYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=iN0JztWgLCh5QVpOqC4acWKNIkvOSMlfS8pM8lEzJhU=)
I’m asking for your support tonight for a couple of reasons.
First, I need your help to fight back against the GOP’s relentless attacks. Unfortunately, as a proud progressive and openly LGBTQ congresswoman, extra scrutiny and political attacks are part of my reality.

| | Dear Freedom Fighters,

As I speak with Legislative District 2 voters, homelessness is still one of the top societal problems our constituents have asked the legislature to solve. If you have been following the status of the nearly one thousand people living in “The Zone” in downtown Phoenix, some of these unhoused individuals are being shuffled into outlying areas across the Valley, including into our very own district where temporary lodging has been secured at places like La Quinta Inn with on-site case management to help these individuals get back on their feet.

Last year, more than a dozen small business owners whose businesses occupy the Zone filed a public nuisance lawsuit with the Maricopa County Superior Court to force the city to do something about the area. The Zone had become so violent a judge had to step in to tell the City of Phoenix to clean up the blocks south of Jefferson Street between Seventh and 15th Avenues.

Earlier this year, a Maricopa County Superior Court judge hearing this case told the City of Phoenix they had to clear the homeless encampment by a set deadline. So far, the city has invested nearly $20 million to clear this specific encampment with the goal of ensuring people do not return to this area by increasing “patrol and enforcement efforts” as well as posting signs saying “no camping” in this area. The city has helped about 600 people by placing them into shelters or other housing arrangements. The city is also working to open a structured campground that will help house a few hundred people experiencing homelessness.

When I was first elected in November 2018, I had the opportunity to tour the Human Services Campus on multiple occasions to see how successful public-private partnerships are working to end homelessness in Phoenix. There are quite a few amazing organizations like the Homeless ID Project and St. Joseph the Worker who have been doing yeoman’s work that deserve the recognition and your tax credit dollars when you file your Arizona taxes.

Last month, my now 19-year-old daughter wrote a paper for one of her ASU Barrett, the Honors College discourse essays called “Sheltering Hope.” In honor of her birthday today, I thought I would include an excerpt from this essay having been a volunteer this past semester with CASS:
_“Silence filled the air as countless families piled their children into makeshift tents, draped with tarps and blankets. Dust swarms dared to wash over the camping stoves and small bonfires fueled by newspaper and scraps of cardboard as multiple families huddled together. Recluses_ _stumbled along the street, glaring at cars as they cautiously passed through the street lined with litter and sleeping bags. Signs that read “Don’t Support Panhandlers” and “There is Another Way to Help” filled each block. Families eagerly awaited–sometimes for weeks at a time–by the side of Central Arizona Shelter Services (CASS) for ample beds open. Until then, they secured leftovers from the kitchen volunteers and stocked up on cans from local donors.”_

It is worth noting, Maricopa County alone has received $500 million to address homelessness since 2019. Over the past two legislative sessions these are some of the dollars set aside to help address the unhoused across the State of Arizona through grants:

**FY 2023**
* $82.4 million allocated to housing and homeless related projects
* $10 million allocated to develop foster youth transitional housing option to the East Valley of Technology (EVIT) to construct a 64-bed transitional housing facility for foster youth
* $2.4 million to construct additional homeless veterans housing in Prescott near Fort Whipple
* $20 million supplemental deposit into the newly created Homeless Shelter and Services Fund. Last year, this grant program awarded grants to the following cities: the City of Phoenix received $7 million, the City of Tucson received $2 million, the City of Glendale received $195,000, the City of Sierra Vista received $52,300, and the City of Flagstaff received $30,000 in matching funds to address homelessness

**FY 2024**

* $210 million was sent to the general fund to address general housing and homelessness
* $7 million targeted at individuals leaving state prisons
* $5 million for a new program targeting homeless veterans
* $40 million deposited into the Homeless Shelter and Services Fund—a grant program for cities to apply like they did in FY 2023 with work done by local nonprofits.
* $31 million went towards gap financing for 16 new housing projects
* $6 million allocated to St. Vincent de Paul to expand their facilities
* $4.7 million allocated to the YMCA for their homeless youth drop-in center
* $1 million awarded to New Freedom in Phoenix for transitional housing apartments
* $10 million set aside for a grant program as a 50% funding match for cities that establish a program that allows homeless individuals to be compensated for daily work and allows homeless individuals participating in this grant program to have access to support services (i.e., Glendale partners with Maricopa County with their Glendale Works program. The City of Glendale partners with the Phoenix Rescue Mission to help homeless individuals gain job experience to get back on their feet)

I look forward to continuing to work for you at the Capitol when we return in January. I have been busy working on legislation brought forth by citizens like you in the coming session.

Best,

Kat Cammack is serving her second term representing the people of Northeastern Florida in Congress. She won the seat on a conservative platform of growing jobs, securing our southern border, standing up for law enforcement, defending our Second Amendment, promoting fiscal responsibility, and defending life.
Congresswoman Cammack sits on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and House Committee on Agriculture, where she is the only Florida Republican serving the Sunshine State's farmers, ranchers, and producers. She was also appointed to the Select Subcommittee on the Weaponization of the Federal Government.
Kat and her husband Matt, who is a firefighter, paramedic, and SWAT medic, proudly call Gainesville, Florida home.

body:
#
With just a few hours left before the end of November, our team is working overtime to reach out to supporters and help us reach our fundraising goal. So we’re coming to you with an important ask:
**Can we count on you to make a contribution of $5 or anything that makes sense to you to help us power this campaign and continue supporting Alexandria’s work in Congress?**
You can make a contribution to our campaign by using this personalized link: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/aoc-email-20231130?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/21874?c0=aoc-email-20231130.bmy2jl&personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com&refcode=em20231130-5403-P_FND_EOM_GOL&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=5403%2E2526796%2EPyPiCf)
_Please use the links in this email to start a monthly donation._
From funding impactful mutual aid efforts like our backpack and turkey drives to building resources to make local and community-focused impacts — _our work is making a difference in more ways than one._
In Congress, Alexandria has been able to remain 100% focused on fighting for our values and calling out bad actors who are trying to drag our progress back. And that's entirely thanks to grassroots support.
**It’s clear that this work will take all of us.** Alexandria is counting on this collective effort.
**If you’re with us, please consider using the personal link below to make a $5, $10, $20 contribution, or whatever you can afford to give before our end-of-month deadline at midnight tonight.**

Team AOC

| I am the daughter of legal immigrants from a small, rural town in South Carolina. We were the only Indian family in our town. My father wore a turban as he still does to this day, and my mother wore a sari. No one knew who we were, what we were, or why we were there. But with each passing day, the community began to look beyond our skin color. They began to see my family for who we are: hard working people who held the same values they cherished. Gradually, those initial stares transformed into smiles and we shifted from being excluded to embraced. Not every day was perfect. But every day was better than the one before it.

---
After graduating from Clemson and working in the corporate world, I decided to take a job working for my family's business that my mother started in our living room when I was a child. I was frustrated when I saw how hard it was to make a dollar and how easy it was for government to take it away. When I voiced these frustrations to my mom, she gave me some wise advice which was: _" Don't complain. Do something about it." _

---
| | | So, that's exactly what I did and I decided to run for state legislature. But it wasn't easy. I ran against the longest-serving legislator in the state and hardly anyone thought I had a chance. I was polling at 15 percent a week before the primary. **But the people of South Carolina took a chance on me, and we won. ➡️**

It was an honor to serve the people as a state legislator. I fought against the status quo and stood up for the people of my district. When I fought for government transparency by pushing to make sure important votes were on the record, my colleagues retaliated. They stripped me of my committees. So I decided to run for governor.

When I campaigned for governor, people didn't know who I was. I was polling in fourth place, with limited time until Election Day. I was the least funded and least known GOP candidate. But together, we defied expectations and won. Then, we made a difference in South Carolina by cutting taxes, creating thousands of jobs, and revitalizing our economy.

When I was nominated as Ambassador to the United Nations, people said I didn't have the experience. I proved them wrong. When I got to the UN, I took the "kick me" sign off our back. I told the world that America would have the backs of our allies, and for those who did not have our backs, we were taking names! The dictators, murderers, and thieves at the UN didn't know what hit them.

My father wore a turban as he still does to this day, and my mother wore a sari. No one knew who we were, what we were, or why we were there. But with each passing day, the community began to look beyond our skin color. They began to see my family for who we are: hard working people who held the same values they cherished. Gradually, those initial stares transformed into smiles and we shifted from being excluded to embraced. Not every day was perfect. But every day was better than the one before it. After graduating from Clemson and working in the corporate world, I decided to take a job working for my family's business that my mother started in our living room when I was a child. I was frustrated when I saw how hard it was to make a dollar and how easy it was for government to take it away. When I voiced these frustrations to my mom, she gave me some wise advice which was: " Don't complain. # FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
NOVEMBER 30, 2023
CONTACT: press@kevinfaulconer.com

**The Building Industry Association of San Diego Endorses Former Mayor Kevin Faulconer for County Supervisor**
SAN DIEGO, CA -- Former San Diego Mayor Kevin Faulconer, candidate for San Diego County Supervisor, announced the backing of the Building Industry Association of San Diego. The latest endorsement continues to build momentum for Faulconer’s campaign as he seeks to represent the residents of the third district. The Building Industry Association (BIA) of San Diego has been the region’s leading voice of residential development for more than 85 years. The BIA is an inclusive member-driven non-profit advocating for housing at all levels and the people and families who need a place to call home. They support pro-housing policies, quality jobs, and help to establish strong communities throughout the region. “Kevin Faulconer is our choice for Supervisor,” said **Lori Holt Pfeiler, President and CEO of BIA San Diego**. “Kevin has a clear record of results as Mayor, is the best choice for Supervisor in District 3, and will bring common-sense policies to the benefit of all communities in San Diego. We trust he has what it takes to bring our region to the next level as we seek to build strong flourishing communities.” “I’m honored to be receiving the endorsement of the Building Industry Association of San Diego” said **Former San Diego Mayor Kevin Faulconer**. “When I was Mayor, our goal was to listen to our communities and work across the aisle to put policies in place that helped support local jobs and local businesses. We put together common-sense housing policies that helped create more development throughout San Diego in areas that sought that development. I’ll bring this experience and solutions driven thinking to the county as Supervisor.” As Mayor of San Diego, Faulconer revised the city’s approach to housing regulation, treating housing as “essential” while making it faster and easier to build in areas across the City that wanted new housing and adopting reforms that cut unnecessary barriers that stood in the way of progress. Under his leadership, the City removed expensive parking minimums and increased citywide housing capacity by 100,000 units after completing 16 community plan updates – more than any administration in City history.
_Former San Diego Mayor Kevin Faulconer is a proven leader with a proven record working to enact common sense solutions to solve some of the region’s most significant issues, including housing, homelessness, and public safety._

They support pro-housing policies, quality jobs, and help to establish strong communities throughout the region. “Kevin Faulconer is our choice for Supervisor,” said Lori Holt Pfeiler, President and CEO of BIA San Diego. “Kevin has a clear record of results as Mayor, is the best choice for Supervisor in District 3, and will bring common-sense policies to the benefit of all communities in San Diego. We trust he has what it takes to bring our region to the next level as we seek to build strong flourishing communities.” “I’m honored to be receiving the endorsement of the Building Industry Association of San Diego” said Former San Diego Mayor Kevin Faulconer. “When I was Mayor, our goal was to listen to our communities and work across the aisle to put policies in place that helped support local jobs and local businesses. We put together common-sense housing policies that helped create more development throughout San Diego in areas that sought that development. I’ll bring this experience and solutions driven thinking to the county as Supervisor.” As Mayor of San Diego, Faulconer revised the city’s approach to housing regulation, treating housing as “essential” while making it faster and easier to build in areas across the City that wanted new housing and adopting reforms that cut unnecessary barriers that stood in the way of progress. Under his leadership, the City removed expensive parking minimums and increased citywide housing capacity by 100,000 units after completing 16 community plan updates – more than any administration in City history. Former San Diego Mayor Kevin Faulconer is a proven leader with a proven record working to enact common sense solutions to solve some of the region’s most significant issues, including housing, homelessness, and public safety. | | | | | Paid for by Faulconer for Supervisor 2024 - FPPC ID 1461674 Want to change how you receive these emails? # **Undercover Investigation Reveals Congressman Costa’s Office Withheld Knowledge of China Bio-Lab from the Public**

An undercover report by O'Keefe Media Group reveals that Congressman Jim Costa’s staff “knew for a few months before anyone else did” about a secret Chinese bio-lab operating in Reedley, California. According to reports, the bio-lab contained deadly pathogens, including Ebola, Malaria, and HIV. Watch the revealing undercover video here:
---
| [ ](https://michaelmaher.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=6239b7d9cb3ad9388556be8be&id=a4b8ff4fe3&e=1722d05e10)
---
| So the question is, what did Congressman Jim Costa know about this Chinese bio-lab, and when did he know it?

Former FBI Special Agent and local businessman Michael Maher noted, “This highlights the need for a new experienced generation to take the helm and lead. As a former Special Agent, I know there is no excuse for delaying the response for months. As your representative, I will support our local elected officials who are pushing federal agencies to ensure that public health and safety are not sidelined.

“Further, more attention must be paid to China’s foreign influence operations, espionage, and organized criminal activities here in California and across this country. For example, the apparent corruption of Gavin Newson’s administration giving over a billion dollars to the Chinese electric car company BYD to produce face masks for COVID-19. Chinese political espionage and foreign influence operations have led elected politicians to hand over taxpayers’ money in subsidies and sweetheart deals to companies like BYD and the Reedley Bio-Lab company.

“The threat posed by the Communist Party of China and its influence is real. We are at war, a new Cold War against the fragile dictators of that authoritarian state who are globally exploiting digital influence and mass surveillance for complete control over people's lives. This is directly at odds with the liberty and freedoms afforded in the Constitution of the United States of America and why we must be vigilant in its defense.

“Jim Costa and his office need to be fully transparent about what they knew and when they knew it, and they also need to be held accountable for needlessly endangering the safety of local residents.”
---
|
---
| _**Background** : Michael Maher is a former FBI Special Agent and US Navy Veteran who was raised in the Central Valley. Michael and his wife, Ann, are raising their young family in Fresno County, and he owns and operates an aviation business. Michael was the 2022 nominee for California's 21st Congressional District._

Ron DeSantis comes from blue-collar roots in the state of Florida. Nothing was handed to him, he worked his way through college and led his team as the Yale Baseball captain. After earning his undergraduate degree, Ron DeSantis graduated from Harvard Law School, but was so moved by the events of September 11, 2001, that he volunteered to serve in the Navy to fight for our freedom. When he returned, he started a life of public service by serving Florida as both Congressman and now Governor. Despite all his years of fighting to ensure the American people enjoy the freedom we're promised in this country, he's watched the Left strip away freedoms at every turn and impose radical agendas on children, families, and consumers nationwide. In 2009, Ron met the love of his life Casey in Florida, and he's now the proud father of 6, 5, and 3-year-old children. Because of his kids, Ron DeSantis knows that this fight is _personal_ and understands the frustration parents face when teachers' unions and liberal groups shove a political agenda down the throats of children.

On Day One, Ron DeSantis has _promised_ that he will bring a RECKONING for what unelected bureaucrats like Anthony Fauci and DC elites have done to children. Ron DeSantis will ignite our Great American Comeback by _immediately getting to work_ stopping the invasion across our southern border, ensuring our military once again puts the mission first, declaring our economic independence, and restoring our American energy dominance so that our country gets back on track before it's too late. In Florida, Ron DeSantis' record speaks for itself. He's taken on the political establishment, politicized bureaucratic agencies, woke corporations, and the legacy media countless times and **_won every single time_**. Under his leadership, Florida has cultivated a thriving economy. It has stood as a citadel of freedom, and with him as our next President, America can once again be that shining City on a Hill for the rest of the world to look upon. _That's why he's running for President of the United States. Ron DeSantis knows that the decline of our country is a choice that cannot continue for another four years; the time to lead is now.... the time to act is now._

Two days later, our congressman voted to overturn the ACA. That was the final straw for me, so I packed up my office and left the job I love to run for Congress. Since the day I was sworn into Congress, I’ve worked to protect the ACA, lower the cost of prescription drugs, and expand access to health care. But we have a lot of work ahead of us. Kim

body:
Hey! Wanted to bump my email to you from yesterday. There are still a few hours left to help us hit our November fundraising goal! Can you chip in? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20231130-2?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20231130-2?refcode=EMAN23_2_PRO_20231130_V1_F&refcode2=33998_3422442_bxPDwS&akid=33998%2E3422442%2EbxPDwS)
* * *
_From: info@katieporter.com
Subject: personally reaching out
Sent: Wednesday, November 29, 2023
_
Hi Derek,
I wanted to provide a quick update, now that we’re less than 100(!) days to our primary election.
I’ve been traveling the state connecting with Californians from all walks of life. From visiting with street vendors in LA, to talking with farm workers in the Central Valley, to meet and greets in San Francisco and Santa Cruz. I LOVE campaigning and hearing from Californians, and grassroots support has made all of these events possible.
**We’ve also been able to run digital ads ([you can check out our first ad here](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20231130-2?refcode=EMAN23_2_PRO_20231130_V1_F&refcode2=33998_3422442_bxPDwS&akid=33998%2E3422442%2EbxPDwS)),** which are an effective and efficient way to reach the millions of undecided California voters who will decide this race.
But now, things are about to really heat up. We’re filming our first TV ad soon, and finalizing our digital and TV ad buys. Buying ad time in California is not cheap, in fact it’s 13x more expensive in parts of California than in other parts of the country.
I’m doing my best to stretch every dollar further, **but polling shows us a third of voters are undecided about who they’ll support.** That means we must do serious work to show voters what I’m all about, and why I’m the best candidate for the job.
Ahead of our November fundraising deadline, I’m wondering if you could make your first donation to our Senate campaign. I’d be so grateful to earn your support. Because I don’t take corporate PAC or federal lobbyist money, your contributions truly are what power this campaign. Here’s a personal link you can use: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20231130-2?personal=dpwillis67@gmail.com](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/kp4s-em-20231130-2?refcode=EMAN23_2_PRO_20231130_V1_F&refcode2=33998_3422442_bxPDwS&akid=33998%2E3422442%2EbxPDwS)
Thanks so much,
Katie Porter

* [Receive Fewer Emails](https://act.katieporter.com/signup/receive-fewer-kp4s-emails/?t=1&akid=33998%2E3422442%2EbxPDwS)

* [Unsubscribe](https://act.katieporter.com/unsubscribe/kp4s-unsubscribe/?t=2&akid=33998%2E3422442%2EbxPDwS)

To give by check:
Katie Porter for Senate

Irvine, CA 92616
